Fact: design_rationale
What to find: How and why key design choices in training were made.
Card sections that often contain it: Training, Design

Answer with status, value, quotes and section.

answer.value: The card gives some rationale for training choices: a multi-stage pipeline (pre-training base, SFT, RL) "progressively unlocks reasoning, tool use, and instruction-following capabilities". SFT uses instruction-following, chain-of-thought and reasoning data to cultivate reasoning and thinking abilities. For the 30B model, a second SFT phase up-sampled agentic data with a smaller share of general replay data. RL uses GRPO across many environments, with verifiable rewards where possible and a generative reward model for open-ended prompts. Asynchronous RL runs generation and policy updates on separate GPU pools rather than in lockstep. A final RLHF phase tunes helpfulness, conversational quality, and safety.
quotes: Granite-4.2-8B is post-trained from [Granite-4.1-8B-Base](https://huggingface.co/ibm-granite/granite-4.1-8b-base) through a rigorous multi-stage pipeline that progressively unlocks reasoning, tool use, and instruction-following capabilities.
The SFT stage draws on instruction-following, chain-of-thought, and reasoning data to cultivate the model's reasoning and thinking abilities.
For the 30B model, we conducted a second SFT phase, in which the agentic data was up-sampled while a smaller share of general replay data was retained.

Most environments provide verifiable rewards, while open-ended prompts are scored by a generative reward model. Training runs asynchronously: generation and policy updates occupy separate GPU pools rather than proceeding in lockstep, and weights are refreshed in flight.
After the reward-driven phases, a preference-alignment (RLHF) phase tunes helpfulness, conversational quality, and safety.
